title: [Bug] KubeRay not compatible with CUDA MPS of NVIDIA device plugin for Kubernetes
body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues) and found no similar issues.


### KubeRay Component

ray-operator

### What happened + What you expected to happen

I configured GPU sharing provided by [NVIDIA device plugin](https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-device-plugin), with configuration like the following:
```
version: v1
sharing:
  mps:
    resources:
    - name: nvidia.com/gpu
      replicas: 10
```
And then I declared resource usage in the worker pod Spec of RayService CRD/RayCluster CRD like:
```
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  requests:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```
The problem is, in any of the worker pod I cannot access GPU when using torch:
```
>>> import torch
>>> torch.cuda.is_available()
/home/ray/anaconda3/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/cuda/__init__.py:129: UserWarning: CUDA initialization: Unexpected error from cudaGetDeviceCount(). Did you run some cuda functions before calling NumCudaDevices() that might have already set an error? Error 205: mapping of buffer object failed (Triggered internally at /pytorch/c10/cuda/CUDAFunctions.cpp:109.)
  return torch._C._cuda_getDeviceCount() > 0
False
```

But nvida-smi shows that GPU is available on the pod. And if I initialize a ray cluster for a scratch (not using ray-operator/RayService CRD/RayCluster CRD, just run pure pods and call `ray start` command in the container entry), I can get access to shared GPU with MPS enabled.

Another interesting point is if I use time-slicing mode, KubeRay can get access to GPU.
```
version: v1
sharing:
  timeSlicing:
    resources:
    - name: nvidia.com/gpu
      replicas: 10
```

### Reproduction script

> helm upgrade -i nvdp nvdp/nvidia-device-plugin --values nvidia-device-plugin.yaml 
```
# nvidia-device-plugin.yaml 
version: v1
sharing:
  mps:
    resources:
    - name: nvidia.com/gpu
      replicas: 10
```
In the worker pod Spec of RayService CRD/RayCluster CRD:
```
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  requests:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```

### KubeRay Component

### What happened + What you expected to happen

I've been trying to use Kuberay Operator to deploy distributed Vllm model inference, utilizing both tensor parallelism and pipeline parallelism. However, through many attempts, I've never managed to run it properly. The closest I've got to running it was by using Rayservice manifest I've attached below.

1) Ray returns error saying that current node has no GPU available. However this is not true, GPU are indeed present in the pod. `nvidia-smi` returns both my GPUs, `torch.cuda.device_count()` also shows 2 gpus available, the exact amount of pod requested resources. Running `ray status` on either of nodes also shows all 4 GPUS available in cluster. GPUs are also visible inside the `Cluster` tab of Ray Dashboard.

title: [Bug] Ray Dashboard breaks running k8s locally in kind w/ prometheus + grafana configured
body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues) and found no similar issues.


### KubeRay Component

Others

### What happened + What you expected to happen

I followed the documented instructions spread across [here](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/cluster/kubernetes/getting-started/raycluster-quick-start.html) and [here](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/cluster/kubernetes/k8s-ecosystem/prometheus-grafana.html) to run kuberay locally w/ metrics configured:

1. Start Kubernetes cluster with kind - `kind create cluster --image=kindest/node:v1.26.0`
2. Deploy KubeRay operator
```
helm repo add kuberay https://ray-project.github.io/kuberay-helm/
helm repo update
helm install kuberay-operator kuberay/kuberay-operator --version 1.3.0
```
3. Pull 1.3.0 repo of KubeRay (match of operator version) - `git checkout 8ba2b33c358ccb515162333ea483263077057b57`
4. Install prometheus & grafana from install scripts - `./install/prometheus/install.sh`
5. Updated image tag in kuberay/ray-operator/config/samples/ray-cluster.embed-grafana.yaml file to use image: `rayproject/ray:2.41.0-aarch64` (ARM-compatible image) for both head node and worker node
6. Created RayCluster - `kubectl apply -f ray-operator/config/samples/ray-cluster.embed-grafana.yaml`
7. Enable port forwarding
```
kubectl port-forward deployment/prometheus-grafana -n prometheus-system 3000:3000
kubectl port-forward raycluster-kuberay-head-rzjnl 8080:8080
kubectl port-forward prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 -n prometheus-system 9090:9090
kubectl port-forward service/raycluster-kuberay-head-svc 8265:8265
```
8. Login to grafana and Import grafana dashboards from kuberay/config/grafana directory
9. Access Ray Dashboard metrics at http://localhost:8265/#/metrics

If I click around in the dashboard and go back to the metrics page several times, I start to see performance degradations, sometimes resulting in a fully broken dashboard. Looking at the port-forwarding logs, I see many instances of errors like:

- `E0320 10:45:24.328848   20682 portforward.go:351] "Unhandled Error" err="error creating error stream for port 3000 -> 3000: Timeout occurred"`
- `E0326 16:06:16.638426   20175 portforward.go:391] "Unhandled Error" err="error copying from remote stream to local connection: readfrom tcp4 127.0.0.1:3000->127.0.0.1:49839: write tcp4 127.0.0.1:3000->127.0.0.1:49839: write: broken pipe"`
- `E0326 15:58:05.048879   20175 portforward.go:404] "Unhandled Error" err="error copying from local connection to remote stream: writeto tcp4 127.0.0.1:3000->127.0.0.1:49347: read tcp4 127.0.0.1:3000->127.0.0.1:49347: read: connection reset by peer"`

Obviously port-forwarding is a contrived / local-dev only feature but it's important to be able to get a minimal setup configured simply to support early explorations of KubeRay / Ray. If there is an alternative path to a more stable option than relying on port-forwarding, then that should be documented instead.

### What happened + What you expected to happen

I have an Openshift cluster equipped with 3 master nodes and 3 worker nodes. All worker nodes are equipped with 2 x L40s GPUs I'm trying to launch a model with distributed inference using 2 worker pods with 1 GPU each.

I have successfully deployed vllm with ray on a vanilla kubernetes cluster with similar configuration (3 master & 3 worker with 2 x L40s GPU) following this [guide](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/cluster/kubernetes/examples/vllm-rayservice.html). For instance, pods, services, secrets and service accounts kept getting automatically generated and terminated.

- `MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "proxy-tls-secret" : secret "llama-3-8b-raycluster-5tbdl-proxy-tls-secret-abc747ae" not found`

title: [Bug] Inconsistent resource requirement treatment when scheduling pods on EKS Auto Mode node pools
body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues) and found no similar issues.


### KubeRay Component

ray-operator

### What happened + What you expected to happen


I am trying to set up a Ray cluster on an EKS Auto Mode cluster with auto-scaling using node pools. Following recommendations in KubeRay documentation, I am aiming for each node to have exactly one Ray pod scheduled on it which will manage all of the node's CPUs.

I am seeing an inability for KubeRay pods to be scheduled on my node pools, even though the resource requests of those pods is lower than the node pool instances provide.

For example, in the cluster created by the reproduction config below, the head pod fails to schedule with the error:
```
incompatible with nodepool "ray-debug-head", daemonset overhead={"pods":"0"}, no instance type has enough resources, requirements=, resources={"cpu":"1500m","memory":"512Mi","pods":"1"};
```
However, the nodepool provides an m5.large instance which has 2 vCPUs.

Note that this can be sidestepped in some cases by specifying lower resource requirements. In the above example, the pod successfully schedules if I reduce the explicit requirement for the head container from 1 CPU to 800m. The issue with specifying too low requirements however is that it can result in multiple pods scheduled on the same node

Moreover, I am unable at all to schedule any head or worker pod on a node with only 1 vCPU, even when I explicitly specify a resource request of 0 CPUs.

I have observed this issue across different EC2 instances and for both head and worker Ray pods. In some cases (with some EC2 instance types), like in the example given above, I can deterministically reproduce the issue and I can fine tune the resource requirement so as to allow the pod to schedule on the desired node while preventing multiple pods scheduling on the same node. In other cases, the issue appears only occasionally even when the Ray cluster and nodepool configuration is kept the same.

I have observed no such issue when creating my own pod with equal resource requirements as the problematic Ray pods - my own pods get successfully scheduled on nodes from the same node pools used by the Ray cluster.

title: [Feature] Add `force` to worker group `suspend` API
body:
### Search before asking

- [X] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues) and found no similar feature requirement.


### Description

https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/pull/2663 adds an API to `suspend` a worker group, and @rueian is working on https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues/2666 to avoid Autoscaler scaling up the suspending or suspended worker groups unexpectedly.

For RayJob, it's fine for KubeRay to kill worker Pods directly. However, we want to expose the suspend API of worker groups to users so that they can also terminate a worker group using the API.

In that case, it seems better to delegate the responsibility of shutting down the Ray pods to the Ray Autoscaler, as it can drain the Ray Pods.

This issue proposes an API change:

```yaml
suspendOptions:
  force: bool
  timeout: int # only effective when `force` is false
```

* Case 1: `force: true`
  * When `force` is set to true, KubeRay kills the pods directly, and the Ray Autoscaler simply avoids scaling the worker group up or down. The RayJob should fall into this category.
  * It is a bit tricky in the case where the Ray Autoscaler doesn’t handle `suspend` because the Ray Autoscaler will still try to update RayCluster CR after `suspend` is set to true. RayCluster controller should not create any Ray Pod for the worker group when `suspend` is set to true.

* Case 2: `force: false`, `timeout` is not set.
  * Case 2-1: Autoscaler is enabled
    * Autoscaler with the handling of `suspend`: Autoscaler drains the Ray Pods, and scales down the Ray Pods.
    * Old Ray versions: Undefined behavior. Users should avoid it.
  * Case 2-2: Autoscaler is not enabled
    * This is not supported. RayCluster spec validation should detect it and create a Kubernetes event.

* Case 3: `force: false`, `timeout` is set.
  * Case 3-1: Autoscaler is enabled
    * Autoscaler with the handling of `suspend`: Autoscaler drains the Ray Pods, and scales down the Ray Pods. If Ray Autoscaler doesn't scale down within `timeout`, KubeRay deletes these Pods.
    * Old Ray versions: Undefined behavior. Users should avoid it.
  * Case 3-2: Autoscaler is not enabled
    * (1) This is not supported. RayCluster spec validation should detect it and create a Kubernetes event.
    * (2) KubeRay deletes these Pods after `timeout`.
    * Both (1) and (2) are fine for me.

Another option is to rely on `rayVersion` to check whether the Ray Autoscaler supports `suspend` or not, and it is considered as a CR spec validation error if `suspend` is set to true but the Ray Autoscaler doesn't support `suspend`. Maybe this is easier for us, as we won’t need to maintain behavior that is hard to define.
